title: CanVar-UK: A collaborative platform for germline interpretation in cancer susceptibility genes.
journal: American Journal of Human Genetics 113(10), Oct 2026 (PMID 42727578). Europe PMC: isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, abstract only. An open preprint version (manuscript + supplement docx, CC BY 4.0) is on Zenodo record 19202187, matching medRxiv 10.64898/2026.03.23.26349065.
data_url: https://canvaruk.org/ (web platform only; no bulk download, export or documented API found). Functional-dataset list: https://canvaruk.org/canvar_datasets

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Homepage, /canvar_datasets and /version_update HTML (v2.2). There is no download/export/API link, and the JS shows 'Batch Query' greyed out as 'under development'. Gene menu: 116 genes with Ensembl transcripts. Undocumented per-variant AJAX endpoints work without login: /getvariants/<gene> returned 7,590 HGVS strings for BAP1 (autocomplete list only). For one variant each, /result/<gene>/<hgvs>/getSummary|getInsilico|getCF|getFA|getGE returned JSON/HTML with hg19/hg38 coordinates, REVEL/BayesDel/CADD/SIFT/PolyPhen/MAPP/SpliceAI scores, gnomAD v4.1/UKB/1000G counts, NDRS NHS case counts with denominators (BRCA1 c.181T>G: 56 of 86,130 tested), and Waters 2024 BAP1 SGE class/score/FDR. The datasets page lists 46 functional, 6 splicing and 12 genetic-epidemiology dataset rows across 19 genes; the listed per-dataset counts sum to 128,882 functional readouts (not deduplicated). I exported 2 of the 8 CanVIG-UK validation Google Sheets: they are assay-level PS3/BS3 calibration summaries (OddsPath, truthset counts), not variant tables. MaveDB API: the BAP1, RAD51C and VHL SGE score sets that CanVar-UK displays are openly downloadable there under CC BY 4.0.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the AJHG abstract: >1.1M SNVs in 116 CSGs, 11 in silico tools, 47 functional/splicing datasets across 19 CSGs, and >1,500 forum users. From the Zenodo preprint docx: 1,744,860 variants, all coding SNVs +25 bp intronic/UTR; NDRS counts from 17 English labs released twice a year; only the forum and lab-stratified counts are password-controlled; per-variant PDF report export. The paper has no data availability statement offering a bulk release. I did not open the AJHG version.

a1_downloadable.note: Fails. Pages are publicly viewable per variant, but there is no bulk download, export, batch query or documented API. Building a table means about 1.1-1.7M variants x 3-5 undocumented endpoints, i.e. scraping an NHS clinical service, which the project rules forbid. Forum classifications (the platform's unique expert labels) need registration and manual credential checks. Note: the unauthenticated getCF JSON also returned per-laboratory NHS count fields that the paper says are password-controlled. I did not collect them.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no native label column. The candidate labels are live-linked ClinVar calls (external), functional classes from 46 separate assays (heterogeneous; originals are in MaveDB/supplements), and forum classifications (login-only). A pathogenicity or case-control label would have to be constructed by joining across sources.

a3_inputs_present.note: Verified on single variants: hg19/hg38 coordinates, ref/alt, HGVS c./p. and Ensembl transcript are present, so sequences can be derived. Most of the 'features' are other tools' predictions (REVEL, CADD, BayesDel, SpliceAI).

a4_units_stated.note: In silico score ranges are labelled (e.g. REVEL [0-1], CADD [0-99]), and counts come with denominators. But functional readouts use each assay's own scale (SGE function score + FDR, HDR, MMR, TP53 yeast/cell assays), with no common unit. I checked one assay (Waters 2024 BAP1) only.

a5_enough_rows.note: From the datasets page listing (not files): 128,882 functional readouts across 19 genes, and the paper says 1,744,860 annotated variants. None of these could be downloaded as rows, so n_rows is null.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Unknown; plausibly ~1-2 GB if the full per-variant table existed. The functional subset is <100 MB as MaveDB CSVs.
a6_fits_laptop.note: Size is not the problem. Access is.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Counts disagree across versions: the AJHG abstract says >1.1M SNVs, 116 genes, 47 datasets in 19 genes. The preprint abstract says >1.7M SNVs, 115 genes, 31 studies in 13 genes. The preprint body says 1,744,860 variants in 116 genes. The website lists 46+6 dataset rows in 19 genes. This is a live database (v2.2), and with no bulk file the counts can't be reconciled.

a8_label_provenance.note: The obvious target (ClinVar/expert pathogenicity) is assigned under ACMG rules that use PP3/BP4 (the same in silico scores shown as features), PS3/BS3 (the same functional readouts) and PS4/BA1 (the same case/population counts). That is leakage by construction. The CanVIG-UK benign truthsets (AJHG 2025) are also built partly from in silico benign evidence. Only the raw functional readouts are physical measurements, and those come from MaveDB, not from this platform.

existing_models.name: In silico predictors already shown on the platform (REVEL, BayesDel, CADD v1.4/v1.6, SIFT, PolyPhen-2, MAPP, Align-GVGD, SpliceAI, HCI priors)
existing_models.score_and_split: The platform reports no performance figures. These tools are the features, not a baseline result.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Paper: prioritising developer time to import 'the large number of small functional assays', and future 'assay-level (and even variant-level) evidence scoring' of MAVE data.

existing_models.name: AlphaMissense and dbNSFP v4.7 predictors + FoldX on AlphaFold2 structures, benchmarked on BRCA1/BRCA2/PALB2/RAD51C (CSBJ 2024, PMID 39430403)
existing_models.score_and_split: AlphaMissense average AUC 0.890 (ordered regions, 4 genes) against HDR assay classes + ClinVar. FoldX on AF2 structures: BRCT AUC 0.861, BRCA2 DBD AUC 0.836. No held-out-gene split.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Most missense variants in these genes remain unclassified; stability alone does not beat dedicated missense predictors.

existing_models.name: Integrated VarCall Model combining two BRCA2 SGE studies (Nat Commun 2026, 10.1038/s41467-026-71393-0)
existing_models.score_and_split: 98.8% accuracy on 6,383 BRCA2 DBD variants against known classifications. Single gene/domain.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not stated in abstract beyond improving functional-evidence accuracy for ACMG use.

existing_models.name: Benign truthset framework for MAVE calibration (Rowlands et al., AJHG 2025, PMID 40925377; same group). A statistical framework, not ML.
existing_models.score_and_split: Using ClinVar benign sets, only 23/116 (19.8%) CSGs can reach PS3 'strong'; systematic truthsets reach strong in 7/8 HBOC genes.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Benign missense truthsets are too small in most genes to calibrate MAVEs.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (only for the salvage route on MaveDB SGE data; nothing in CanVar-UK itself needs a backbone)
backbone.hardware: CPU; ~19 proteins, embeddings cached once in minutes.
backbone.licence: ESM-2 MIT. MaveDB score sets checked are CC BY 4.0. CanVar-UK has no stated data licence.

integration.partner_dataset: n/a for CanVar-UK (no bulk table). Salvage: MaveDB SGE score sets + ClinVar variant_summary.
integration.join_key: hg38 chrom:pos:ref:alt or Ensembl transcript + HGVS c.

controls.positive_control: Not applicable (rejected). For the salvage: nonsense variants must score as LOF in every SGE set.
controls.negative_control: Not applicable (rejected). For the salvage: label shuffle within gene.
controls.external_validation: Not applicable (rejected). For the salvage: NDRS case-count enrichment would be ideal, but there is no bulk release.

honest_claim_h3: Any model built from CanVar-UK aggregates would predict ACMG/ClinVar-style classifications for coding SNVs in 116 UK-tested CSGs, and those classifications were partly assigned from the same in silico, functional and frequency columns used as inputs.
ml_idea: None viable on CanVar-UK itself. The salvage is a different candidate: download the SGE/MAVE score sets for the 19 CSGs directly from MaveDB (CC BY 4.0), fit frozen ESM-2 + head, and test leave-one-gene-out transfer. Check C2 against ProteinGym-style VEP benchmarks first, because the field is crowded.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Done: looked for a bulk export, API or batch query on canvaruk.org. None exists ('Batch Query under development'), and per-variant pages and PDFs are the only output.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: CanVar-UK is a per-variant clinical lookup tool with no bulk download, export or API, and its unique labels (forum classifications) need a credentialed login. A2 and A8 also fail: no native label column, and the natural target (ACMG/ClinVar class) is built from the same in silico, functional and frequency evidence the platform displays. The underlying functional data is openly available from MaveDB, so evaluate that separately.
